state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's think about it this way: imagine you have a set of toy cars, and you double the size of each car. Would the range of the sizes of the cars stay the same? Think about how this analogy relates to what Tom and Katie are saying about the plants.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I think if I double the size of the toy cars, the range would change because everything gets bigger, right? But with Katie's idea of adding \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \), I'm not sure how that affects the range. Can you explain why that would change it too?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's think about it this way: imagine you have a group of friends, and each person grows by 3 inches. Would the range of heights stay the same? How does this relate to Katie's suggestion of adding 3 cm to each plant's height?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I think if all my friends grow by 3 inches, the tallest person would still be the tallest, and the shortest would still be the shortest, so the range would change, right? But I'm still a bit confused about how that works with the plants. Can you explain why both Tom and Katie are wrong?
